title: KV shard allocator and batch-packing optimizer for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Jonah Kim
description: Background: Long-context variants of Llama, Mistral, and Qwen (32k+) are stressing our GPU memory layout and continuous-batching pipeline. Requests with long prefixes increase KV cache residency and produce fragmentation that forces conservative memory reservations or OOMs. Existing heuristics treat all models the same and don't exploit model-specific token-size, kv-shard layout, or quantization profile differences. Goal: Implement a model-aware KV shard allocator plus a batch-packing optimizer that cooperates with continuous batching to maximize slot utilization while minimizing peak GPU resident memory and OOM risk across Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants in long-context configs.
approach: 1) Data collection: gather per-model distributions (seq length, live KV bytes per token for fp16/int8/4-bit), observed prefix reuse rates, and eviction patterns from production traces and synthetic long-context runs. 2) KV shard allocator: implement a per-model allocator that places KV caches in logical shards by lifetime and access frequency. Short-lived prefixes go in compact eviction-friendly shards; long-lived chat sessions pin to stable shards with reserved slots. 3) Batch-packing optimizer: change the continuous-batching planner to pack requests using a knapsack-style heuristic that groups similar live-KV-size requests to reduce padding and peak memory. The planner should consider model, quantization profile, and region. 4) Fragmentation mitigation: add a lightweight compaction/slot-recycler that runs between serving cycles to coalesce free slots under low-latency conditions. 5) Safe rollout: feature-flagged, gated by per-customer memory SLOs and a conservative fallback to current allocator on failure.
acceptance_criteria:
- No increase in error-rate or tail latency for regular 8k workloads.
- Reduce production OOM incidents for long-context requests by >= 90% for targeted models (measured over 7d).
- Decrease average peak GPU resident memory for long-context test harness by >= 28% across Llama-2-70B-chat (32k), Mistral-7B-Long, and Qwen-32k.
- Continuous-batching throughput (tokens/s) does not regress more than 5% for normal traffic mixes.
- End-to-end E2E tests and canary runs pass and rollout is reversible within 15 minutes.
test_plan:
- Offline: run stress harness with synthetic prefixes and mixed quantization (fp16, int8, 4-bit) for each model variant; compare peak memory and throughput.
- Integration: run canary on 10% of dedicated capacity with telemetry enabled (memory histograms, OOMs, latency p95/p99).
- Automated checks: unit tests for allocator correctness, invariant tests for slot accounting, and chaos tests that inject eviction delays.
- Benchmarks: record token/s and mem-peak using runtime-1.20 benchmark harness and compare to baseline runtime-1.19.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: New packing heuristic could increase tail latency for heterogeneous mixes. Mitigation: limit aggressive packing to requests below a latency budget and maintain a fast-path for single-request low-latency flows.
- Risk: Compaction could momentarily increase CPU/GPU overhead. Mitigation: run compaction throttled and only when GPU utilization < 30% or during low-latency windows.
- Risk: Incorrect per-model parameters may hurt some customers. Mitigation: per-customer toggles + rollback + telemetry-driven auto-tune that pulls safe defaults from production traces.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag behind per-cluster gate. 2) Internal dogfood: enable on runtime-dev for two days. 3) Canary: enable on 5% of dedicated pools for Llama and Mistral only, monitor 72h. 4) Expand to include Qwen on success, then to hosted pools progressively. 5) Full rollout after 14-day verification window and customer opt-in for Private deployments. 6) Provide a runtime flag to revert to legacy allocator instantly.
metrics:
- OOM incident count (per-model, per-cluster).
- Peak GPU resident memory (bytes) histogram by model.
- Continuous-batching utilization (packed tokens / allocated slots).
- p95/p99 latency for short and long requests.
- Throughput (tokens/s) for benchmark workloads.
